subject: Dedicated scaling runway and SLO scenario planning for NovaProd
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@novaprod.com>, NovaProd Procurement <procure@novaprod.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-18T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Dedicated scaling runway and SLO scenario planning for NovaProd

Samantha / Procurement team —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per the request from your architecture and procurement leads, I pulled together a near-term dedicated capacity plan that aligns to the 12-month forecast you shared (PDF in HubSpot). High-level summary here and attached spreadsheet with the token/sec scenarios.

Key asks I want us to align on now:
- Confirm target p50/p95 generation latency SLOs for your public-facing API (you mentioned p95 <= 350ms for 2k concurrent users).
- Agree preferred model family (we showed rwkv-13B / redwood-7B / llama-2-13B options) so we can size exact per-token cost and memory; defaults below assume a 13B dense.
- Procurement: confirm preferred billing cadence and whether a 12-month reserved commitment is in scope (we have a better price/guaranteed headroom with annual commits).

Preliminary numbers (attached workbook "capacity_calc_v3.xlsx" has the math):
- Baseline scenario A (steady traffic): 2,000 concurrent users, 25 tokens/request avg, steady-state QPS ~83 requests/sec => ~2,083 tokens/sec.
- Model: 13B quant-4 (H100-opt), average token time 0.45ms/token on H100 with batching 32.
- Effective tokens/sec per GPU (conservative, including KV and prefix penalties): ~65k tokens/sec.
- Required GPUs (A): 2,083 / 65,000 => <0.05 GPUs (rounded up to 1 dedicated slot for HA/burst). We recommend 2 GPUs behind load balancer for redundancy.

Burst scenario B (peak + KV warm):
- Peak concurrent 8,000 users, same token average => 8,333 tokens/sec.
- With typical burst inefficiencies (lower batch efficiency, cold KV cache), effective tokens/sec per GPU drops to ~28k.
- Required GPUs (B): 8,333 / 28,000 => ~0.3 -> recommend 4 GPUs in a reserved pool to keep p95 <= 350ms with headroom.

Headroom and SLO mapping:
- Target p95 <= 350ms requires maintaining median token latencies ~0.35ms/token and keeping batching efficient. That means we need autoscaling triggers at 60% of reserved pool utilization and a burst reserve of 25% capacity.

Operational recommendations:
- Dedicated pool: start with 4x H100 (reserved) with autoscale policy to add burst nodes (shared burst lane) up to 8 GPUs.
- Model variants: deploy a quantized 13B as primary and a 7B as fallback for cost-sensitive routes; route less-urgent workloads to 7B.
- Caching: enable prefix/KV persistent cache for common prefixes (e.g., customer prompts) to cut effective token work by ~15% in steady-state.

I've attached the workbook and a short SLA-runbook (sla_runbook_v2.pdf) that maps autoscale triggers to billing windows. Sergio / Marissa — can you validate the per-GPU tokens/sec assumptions against our H100 fleet perf data and update the spreadsheet?

Next steps:
1) Samantha — confirm p95 target and model choice this week.
2) Procurement — flag whether a 12-month reserved commitment is viable; we can translate to a formal quote after the sizing is validated.
3) Redwood ops (cc'd) will sanity-check the GPU perf numbers and finalize a recommendation.

Thanks,

Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com

Thanks Vanessa — this is helpful. A few clarifying items from our side:

1) SLOs: product is firm on p95 <= 300ms for the customer-facing endpoints; internal tooling can tolerate p95 <= 700ms.
2) Model choice: we prefer the 13B dense as primary but are open to a quantized profile if the quality delta is small. Can you add a quality delta estimate for redwood-13B quant vs dense (L0/L1)?
3) Procurement: we are likely to push for a 9–12 month term; budget lead wants estimated monthly burn for both 4xH100 and 8xH100 reserved pools.

Also looping in our infra lead about networking (they want to confirm egress / PrivateLink options).

—Samantha

samantha.lee@novaprod.com

Subject: Re: Dedicated scaling runway and SLO scenario planning for NovaProd — perf check

Vanessa / Marissa — quick pass on the perf assumptions. I pulled latest bench results from H100 pool and updated capacity_calc_v3.xlsx (tab 'perf_updates'). Notes:

- 13B dense (float16) on H100 with batching=32: 68k tokens/sec (steady), p95 token latency ~0.28ms (good).
- 13B q4_0 on H100 with optimized kernels: ~54k tokens/sec, p95 ~0.36ms. Quality delta: we measured ~2.4% absolute drop on Rouge-L on our internal eval set for q4_0 vs float16; for instruction-following prompts the difference is often negligible but depends on length and sampling.
- Cold KV penalty: first few tokens with small prefixes add ~18% latency overhead until cache warms.
- Real-world effective tokens/sec (accounting for network overhead & safety checks): apply a 0.82 multiplier to bench numbers for conservative planning.

I've attached the updated workbook and added a 'quote-ready' section with 4xH100 and 8xH100 monthly burn estimates (line items for reserved discount tiers). High level:
- 4xH100 (reserved, 12mo): estimated ~$64k/month (baseline, steady).
- 8xH100 (reserved, 12mo): estimated ~$119k/month (supports higher headroom + burst pool).

Recommendation: Given NovaProd's p95 <= 300ms target, plan for 6xH100 as the starting reserved commitment with autoscale up to 12 for seasonal peaks. That gives a comfortable 30–40% headroom and aligns with your 9–12 month procurement window.

I also added runbook snippets to sla_runbook_v2.pdf mapping autoscale hysteresis and circuit-breaker thresholds.

Sergio

Samantha / Procurement — thanks for the prompt feedback. Quick summary and asks so we can push a formal quote tomorrow: 

Summary of what we validated:
- Perf numbers: Sergio updated bench shows H100 float16 ~68k tokens/sec; q4_0 ~54k tokens/sec. After conservative multiplier (0.82) use ~55k and ~44k respectively for planning.
- For p95 <= 300ms target, we recommend a reserved starting commitment of 6x H100 with autoscale to 12x for bursts. This balances cost and headroom and keeps autoscale triggers at ~60% utilization.
- Monthly burn estimates in the updated workbook: 6xH100 reserved ~ $95k/month (12mo, committed). 12x burst-capable pool ~ $185k/month if fully utilized. Exact numbers in the sheet.

Action items:
1) Samantha — confirm model variant preference (13B float16 primary or 13B q4_0 primary with 7B fallback) by end of day tomorrow so we can lock pricing and QoS assumptions.
2) Procurement — if a 12mo commitment is acceptable, flag any commercial exceptions you require (audit, right-to-audit, data residency clauses).
3) Marissa / Sergio — please produce a final quote doc and a short one-page SLO appendix we can attach to the contract.

I'll schedule a 30-min follow-up tomorrow afternoon to run through the final quote if that works for everyone.

Best,
Vanessa
